prompt: 1.Technology is becoming progressively universal. In the fullness of time, classroom teacher will be totally substituted for technology. Do you agree or disagree.
essay:
In the modern world, technological advancements are becoming increasingly influential in many areas of life, including education. Digital tools are now widely used in classrooms to enhance both teaching and learning. However, the view that technology will completely replace human teachers is unconvincing. This essay argues that, although technology can support education, it cannot effectively manage students’ behaviour or provide the human interaction necessary for effective learning.

Firstly, AI-powered teaching systems would lack the authority, judgement and adaptability required to maintain discipline in a classroom. Young learners, in particular, often require close supervision and immediate intervention to remain focused and behave appropriately. Human educators can identify signs of distraction or disruptive behaviour and respond according to the individual circumstances of each student. By contrast, automated teaching systems may struggle to interpret the underlying causes of such behaviour or respond appropriately to unpredictable situations. For example, a teacher may recognise that a student's lack of concentration is caused by confusion, anxiety or a personal difficulty and adjust their approach accordingly. Therefore, relying entirely on technology could make it considerably more challenging to establish and maintain a well-disciplined learning environment.

Secondly, the complete replacement of teachers could have a detrimental effect on the quality of students’ education. Effective teaching involves far more than simply delivering information; learners also need encouragement, motivation and emotional support. Human educators are capable of identifying students’ strengths and weaknesses, adapting their teaching strategies and providing reassurance when learners encounter difficulties. For instance, a student struggling to understand a complex concept may benefit from personalised guidance, encouragement and additional explanations. Although AI-based systems can deliver information quickly and provide personalised academic exercises, they cannot fully replicate the empathy, emotional intelligence and interpersonal connection that human teachers offer. Consequently, eliminating human interaction from the classroom could undermine students’ motivation and negatively affect their overall educational experience.

In conclusion, while technological developments can undoubtedly enhance the educational process, they are unlikely to make human teachers redundant. The inability of automated systems to exercise human judgment in managing behaviour, together with their limitations in providing emotional and interpersonal support, means that educators will continue to play an indispensable role in creating an effective learning environment.
